lesson.title: 27 familiar letters
lesson.theory: Arcon uses the standard Latin alphabet from a to z, plus one extra letter — ū (u with a line on top). Most letters sound almost the same as they do in English or in IPA transcription.

lesson.title: Vowels
lesson.theory: Five familiar vowels, plus the special ū — it sounds like German ü (as in 'über') or French u (as in 'tu'): round your lips as if saying 'oo', but position your tongue as if saying 'ee'.

examples.translation: like German ü (über) or French u (tu)

lesson.prompt: How is the special letter ū pronounced?

lesson.title: Consonants
lesson.theory: Consonants are very predictable (b, d, f, g, l, m, n, p, r, s, t, v, z — as usual), but there are a few worth knowing about:

examples.translation: like the 'ch' in Scottish 'loch' or German 'Bach' — not a sound English uses natively
